concept.title: Figures and diagrams
concept.shortdesc: Figures carry GOV.UK-styled captions, and the DITA SVG domain embeds scalable diagrams that stay crisp at any size.

conbody.p: diagramsSVGA figure whose diagram is referenced through a key — the same mechanism the Open Referral UK publications use for hundreds of model diagrams:
The same diagram referenced directly by path:

Local SVG diagrams are inlined as native SVG, so any links inside a diagram are clickable and the artwork stays crisp at any size. Each image also receives an accessible name derived from the figure title, the caption is numbered automatically, and the diagram never overflows the content column. Set govuk.svg.inline=no to keep the plain image rendering instead.

section.title: Diagrams and the content policy
section.p: An inlined diagram becomes part of the page, so it is treated as code, not as an image. By default the build removes anything in an SVG file that would run or fetch in the reader's browser — script, foreignObject, event-handler attributes, links whose scheme runs code, and images or fragments fetched from another origin — and reports what it found and removed (GOVK004W). Ordinary links to other websites inside a diagram are kept. A publisher who wants the file exactly as authored sets govuk.svg.sanitize=no; the report still appears. Diagrams are inlined only from under the input directory (govuk.inline.scope); a reference that points elsewhere on the build machine is reported and rendered as an image instead. Attributes that arrive only as SVG 1.1 doctype defaults (contentScriptType, zoomAndPan and their kin) are dropped, so tool-generated diagrams validate.

The same policy covers images and objects fetched from another origin and links whose scheme runs code anywhere in a topic: each is reported (GOVK006W), rendered as authored under govuk.content.policy=warn, or replaced by a marked placeholder under strip. Nothing here ever fails a build.
